abstract: The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies asks whether uniform ellipticity implies $H^s$-coercivity for symmetric nonlocal kernels of order $2s$, with $0<s<1$. We show that the conjecture fails whenever $n>2s$ for every $s \in (0,1)$ and $n \geq 1$, even for smooth compactly supported test functions; for $n=1$ and $s>1/2$, we show that it holds. The construction also gives bounded discontinuous weak solutions in $H^s_{\rm loc}$ to nonlocal equations in divergence form with kernels in this class. Despite the failure, we show that the conjecture holds for several important classes of kernels. We establish a general local coercivity criterion based on annular cancellation, which applies in particular to kernels satisfying both divergence- and nondivergence-form symmetry. The criterion also allows us to treat kernels comparable to stable kernels with bounded measurable coefficients, as well as non-cutoff Boltzmann kernels under a geometric nonconcentration assumption. As an application, we obtain a short and self-contained proof of the Gressman--Strain anisotropic coercivity estimate. Furthermore, by combining our new criterion with existing regularity results, we obtain H\"older estimates under ellipticity and cancellation assumptions.
hook: The nonlocal coercivity conjecture is false in general, yet holds for several key kernel classes.

summary: The authors build counterexamples showing that uniform ellipticity does not force H^s coercivity whenever n > 2s, and the same construction gives discontinuous weak solutions. They then prove the claim for several important kernel classes using an annular cancellation criterion, which also gives a short proof of a known anisotropic estimate. The positive results need extra assumptions on the kernels.
title: The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies
